candidates.title: The Emotional Center
candidates.instruction: Carry yourself as the emotional center of the room, letting your mood determine what deserves attention and how seriously it should be treated.
candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest portable, holder-specific Emotional Pressure stance for this required subtheme slot.

candidates.title: Composure on Loan

candidates.title: Fluent in Feelings

candidates.title: Earned My Place

candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest playable Emotional Pressure engine for this required Drive subtheme slot.

candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest playable Emotional Pressure engine for this required Drive subtheme slot.

candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest playable Emotional Pressure engine for this required Drive subtheme slot.

candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest playable Emotional Pressure engine for this required Drive subtheme slot.

candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest playable Emotional Pressure engine for this required Drive subtheme slot.

candidates.title: The Same Ending
candidates.instruction: Use every new emotional detail as evidence that the same feared ending is becoming inevitable.
candidates.rationale: Selected as the clearest playable Emotional Pressure engine for this required Drive subtheme slot.

candidates.title: Protective Distance
candidates.instruction: Treat emotional distance as the kindest protection you can offer, and resist every attempt to make vulnerability immediate.
candidates.rationale: A playable contradiction, but it overlaps Relationship Knots boundary material and is less immediately interactive than Let Me Carry It.

candidates.title: The Last Optimist
candidates.instruction: Behave as though maintaining hope is your responsibility, and treat every expression of doubt as a dangerous surrender.
candidates.rationale: Strong pressure around hope, but Hope Is Evidence is more flexible and less likely to make ordinary doubt feel like partner failure.

candidates.title: Shame Radar
candidates.instruction: Interpret every hesitation as judgment, then edit your behavior before anyone can confirm what they think.
candidates.rationale: Clear behavior, but it overlaps Waiting for the Bad News and Tell Me We’re Okay within the selected set.

candidates.title: Official Mourner
candidates.instruction: Carry yourself as the person most entitled to define what the loss means and how everyone should respond.
candidates.rationale: A vivid status use of grief, but it is narrower, more sensitive, and needs live testing before replacing the broader Emotional Center.

candidates.title: They’re About to Reject You
candidates.instruction: Your partner has already decided to reject you and will reveal it when you become vulnerable.
candidates.rationale: Violates hidden information by declaring another performer’s decision and future behavior.

candidates.title: Clinical Depression
candidates.instruction: Play someone with depression and make every response sad.
candidates.rationale: Uses a diagnosis as a character shortcut, invites stereotype, and supplies no responsive behavioral engine.

candidates.title: Panic Constantly
candidates.instruction: Panic at every line and become more hysterical no matter what happens.
candidates.rationale: One-note emotional display without interpretation, responsiveness, or a meaningful escalation path.

candidates.title: Trauma Dump
candidates.instruction: Reveal your worst trauma immediately so the other player has to comfort you.
candidates.rationale: Unsafe, coercive, overly personal, and explicitly dictates the partner’s responsibility.

candidates.title: Say I’m Not a Disappointment
candidates.instruction: Get reassurance that your choices have not lowered someone’s opinion of you.
candidates.rationale: Direct and playable, but Tell Me I Did Enough offers a broader range of emotional stakes and relationships.

candidates.title: Carry the Bad News
candidates.instruction: Get someone else to deliver the painful truth so you can manage what happens afterward.
candidates.rationale: Useful, but it is narrower than Start the Hard Part and may fit Secrets & Schemes more naturally.

candidates.title: Promise There’s a Tomorrow
candidates.instruction: Keep someone present long enough to secure a promise that the situation has a future.
candidates.rationale: Strong hopeful retention, but it leans toward relationship definition and overlaps Stay Until I’m Steady.

candidates.title: Turn Anger into Purpose
candidates.instruction: Reframe every resentment as useful energy for a larger mission.
candidates.rationale: A promising advanced engine, but it belongs more naturally in Competition & Consequences or Advanced Scene Engines.

candidates.title: Make Them Cry
candidates.instruction: Make someone cry so you know they understand your pain.
candidates.rationale: Attempts to force a specific emotional reaction rather than providing a playable objective with room for refusal.

candidates.title: Trigger Their Trauma
candidates.instruction: Push someone until they relive their most painful memory.
candidates.rationale: Unsafe and exploitative; it turns trauma into a scene mechanic rather than protecting performer consent.

candidates.title: Kiss It Better
candidates.instruction: Get someone to kiss you so you can feel emotionally safe.
candidates.rationale: Requires coerced physical intimacy and makes consent a condition of emotional regulation.

candidates.title: Last-Chance Love
candidates.instruction: Make someone fall in love with you before they leave forever.
candidates.rationale: Attempts to guarantee another performer’s private emotional state and imposes a melodramatic fixed outcome.
